blocks.text: Blu Living Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Blu Living is one townhouse complex at a single address — 15988 32 Avenue in South Surrey, across from Morgan Creek Golf Club — and this page covers that complex only, not a neighbourhood.

The legal frame the City itself uses is the lot at 15988 32 Avenue under Comprehensive Development (CD) By-law No. 16608, with Development Permit No. 7907-0105-00 allowing the townhouse project on the property.
The surrounding plan area is Grandview Heights, which the City guides through the Grandview Heights General Land Use Plan (GLUP) and its neighbourhood concept plans.

blocks.text: Blu Living Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The homes are large detached-form strata townhouses: listing records for the complex describe three-level, five-bedroom townhouses of roughly 2,850 to 2,990 square feet with a ground-level one-bedroom suite — listing-stated figures for individual units, not a developer specification, and flagged as such.

The City's own record fixes the first phase: Corporate Report R086 (May 9, 2011) describes Phase 1 as 10 buildings of townhouse units, with Building 9 (Unit 13) and Building 10 (Unit 14) constructed in 2010 and 2011.

Those two buildings reached Council because they were occupied rental townhouses being converted to strata title — the report is a Strata Title Conversion application under the Strata Property Act, so early Blu Living homes began as rentals and were strata-titled after occupancy.

blocks.text: Blu Living Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The complex is governed by its own CD zone, By-law No. 16608, not a standard Surrey townhouse zone — what can be built, added or altered at 15988 32 Avenue runs through that bylaw and Development Permit No. 7907-0105-00.

Because the first buildings were strata conversions of occupied rentals, a buyer of an early-phase unit should confirm on title that the unit sits in the larger strata the Approving Officer signed off on, exactly as the 2011 report describes the conversion path.

Long-term rental restriction bylaws are unenforceable in British Columbia stratas since November 24, 2022, but the ground-level suites in these homes are part of the unit's own floor plan — renting the suite separately is a strata-bylaw and City secondary-suite question to confirm for the specific unit, not an assumption.

The strata must obtain a depreciation report every five years (stratas of five or more lots, in force July 1, 2024) — for a complex built in phases from 2010 onward, that report is where phase-by-phase envelope and roof timing first shows.

blocks.text: Blu Living Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The complex's own zoning is a one-off: CD By-law No. 16608 was written for this property, so a Blu Living addition, deck or exterior change is judged against that bylaw's text, not the standard townhouse (RM) rules a Surrey buyer may know from other complexes.
Phase 1 alone was 10 buildings — the complex is phased, so two units with the same floor plan can sit in buildings of different ages with different depreciation-report timelines.

The golf course across 32 Avenue is Morgan Creek Golf Club — the address's defining landmark, and the reason the page places the complex as "Townhomes at Morgan Creek" even though board data places it under Grandview Surrey.

Listing records describe a self-contained ground-level suite with its own entrance in these homes — a feature to verify unit by unit on the strata plan and the City suite record, since suite legality is per-unit paperwork, not complex marketing.

Provisional versus final occupancy mattered here at conversion: the City withheld final occupancy approval for Buildings 9 and 10 until engineering servicing and landscaping were finished and approved — the kind of condition a buyer of a converted unit confirms was discharged.
Grandview Heights Secondary at 16987 25 Avenue and the Grandview Corners retail area on 24 Avenue are the local anchors east of the complex.

blocks.text: Blu Living Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Read the CD bylaw before pricing any change: CD By-law No. 16608 and Development Permit No. 7907-0105-00 are the documents that govern this lot, and both are City records a buyer or their lawyer can pull — a standard-zone assumption is the main paperwork risk here.

For a converted rental unit (Phase 1), confirm the strata plan registration and that the conversion conditions in the 2011 Council approval — servicing, landscaping, final occupancy — were completed for that building.
The depreciation report and Form B Information Certificate for the exact phase's strata plan state the planned levies — phases differ in age here, so a complex-wide summary is not enough.

faq.a: The City record names only the zoning (CD By-law No. 16608), the development permit (No. 7907-0105-00) and the phase structure.

faq.q: Were these homes always strata, or were they rentals first?
faq.a: At least the first phase began as rentals. Corporate Report R086 (May 9, 2011) is a strata title conversion application for occupied townhouse units in Buildings 9 and 10, which the City says were constructed in 2010 and 2011, with final occupancy approval held until servicing and landscaping were complete. A buyer should verify their unit's phase and conversion status on title.
Catchments in School District 36 are address-based, so run the exact unit address through the district locator before relying on either public school.

faq.q: Which schools are near Blu Living, by name and address?
faq.a: Morgan Elementary at 3366 156a St and Grandview Heights Secondary at 16987 25 Ave, Surrey, both confirmed in the BC Ministry K-12 file; Southridge School (independent) is at 2656 160 St

faq.q: How large are Blu Living homes?
faq.a: Blu Living has four- and five-bedroom townhomes beside detached strata homes, together ranging from about 2,800 to 3,300 sq ft; confirm the exact size of a specific unit

faq.q: What should a buyer review before buying at Blu Living?
faq.a: The Form B information certificate, the strata bylaws and rules, the last two years of minutes and the depreciation report, plus what the monthly fees cover
